title: What Forms Do Inside LeadProspectrr
moduleName: Forms: Capturing Leads the Right Way
learningGoal: Understand how forms capture leads and start the follow-up process automatically.

items.title: First Step in the Journey
items.description: A form is often the first step in the customer journey. Someone fills out a form to request a consultation, download a guide, join a newsletter, or ask for a quote.

items.title: The Big Mistake
items.description: Many people think the form is the whole process. It is not. A form should start the next action, not end the interaction.

items.title: What LeadProspectrr Can Do
items.description: When someone fills out a form, LeadProspectrr can create a contact, add a tag, send notifications, send thank-you emails, add leads to pipelines, start workflows, and redirect to booking pages.

items.title: Who is this person?
items.description: Capture their name, email, and contact information so you know who they are.

items.title: What do they want?
items.description: Understand their interest, need, or goal so you can help them appropriately.

items.title: What should happen next?
items.description: Trigger the right follow-up: notification, email, pipeline entry, or workflow.

keyPoint: The form collects the lead. The follow-up turns that lead into a conversation. A good form starts a process, not just collects data.

actionSteps.title: Review Your Current Forms
actionSteps.description: Look at any forms you currently use. Do they answer the three questions: Who, What, and What Next?

actionSteps.title: Identify Gaps
actionSteps.description: Where do leads currently enter your business? Email? Contact forms? Direct messages? Spreadsheets?

actionSteps.title: Open LeadProspectrr Forms
actionSteps.description: Navigate to Sites → Forms and explore what is available.

quizzes.question: What is the main purpose of a form in LeadProspectrr?

options.option_text: To collect data and end the interaction
To start the next action and trigger follow-up

quizzes.explanation: A form should start the next action, not end the interaction. It triggers follow-up processes like notifications, emails, and workflows.

quizzes.question: What are the three questions a good form should answer?

options.option_text: Who is this person, What do they want, What should happen next

quizzes.explanation: A good form answers: Who is this person? What do they want? What should happen next? This ensures proper follow-up.

quizzes.question: What can LeadProspectrr do when someone submits a form?

options.option_text: Nothing, it just stores the data
Create contacts, add tags, send notifications, start workflows, add to pipelines

quizzes.explanation: LeadProspectrr can automatically create contacts, add tags, send notifications and emails, add leads to pipelines, start workflows, and redirect to booking pages.

title: When to Use a Form
moduleName: Forms: Capturing Leads the Right Way
learningGoal: Learn the best use cases for forms and when to create different types of forms.

items.title: Contact & Consultation
items.description: Contact forms, consultation requests, discovery call requests. Capture interest from prospects ready to talk.

items.title: Downloads & Signups
items.description: Lead magnet downloads, newsletter signups, guide requests. Build your email list with interested prospects.

items.title: Events & Registration
items.description: Event registration, speaking inquiries, workshop signups. Manage attendance and follow-up for events.

items.title: Business Requests
items.description: Client intake, quote requests, feedback requests. Collect specific information for business processes.

items.title: Do Not Use One Form for Everything
items.description: Different goals need different forms. A consultation form should not look the same as a newsletter signup form.

items.title: Match Form to Purpose
items.description: Create specific forms for specific purposes. This helps with tagging, follow-up, and understanding lead quality.

items.title: Where to Find Forms
items.description: In LeadProspectrr: Sites → Forms. From there you can view, create, edit, preview, and get embed codes.

keyPoint: Use a form when you need to collect information and send it into LeadProspectrr. Create different forms for different purposes—do not use one form for everything.

actionSteps.title: List Your Form Needs
actionSteps.description: Write down all the places where you currently collect lead information.

actionSteps.title: Categorize by Purpose
actionSteps.description: Group them by type: consultation, download, event, quote request, etc.

actionSteps.title: Plan Your Forms
actionSteps.description: Decide how many forms you need and what each one should capture.

nextLessonTitle: What Makes a Good Lead Capture Form

quizzes.question: When should you use a form?

options.option_text: When you need to collect information and send it into LeadProspectrr

quizzes.explanation: Use a form whenever you need to collect information from someone and send it into LeadProspectrr for follow-up and organization.

quizzes.question: Why should you create different forms for different purposes?

options.option_text: Different goals need different fields, tags, and follow-up processes
Forms are free so you should make many

quizzes.explanation: Different forms allow you to capture the right information, apply appropriate tags, and trigger the correct follow-up for each specific purpose.

quizzes.question: Where do you find forms in LeadProspectrr?
quizzes.explanation: Forms are found under Sites → Forms in LeadProspectrr, where you can view, create, edit, and manage all your forms.

title: What Makes a Good Lead Capture Form
moduleName: Forms: Capturing Leads the Right Way
learningGoal: Learn the difference between good and poor forms, and what fields to include.

items.title: Consultation Request Form
items.description: First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone, What service are you interested in?, What is your biggest challenge right now?

items.title: Why It Works
items.description: It is enough to start a useful conversation without overwhelming the prospect. Clear, short, purposeful.

items.title: The Overwhelming Form
items.description: Full address, Company size, Budget, Website, Social media links, Full business history, Ten open-ended questions.

items.title: Why It Fails
items.description: That is too much too soon. People are more likely to complete a form when it feels easy. Long forms reduce responses.

items.title: Basic Fields
items.description: First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone. Start with these for most lead capture forms.

items.title: Interest Field
items.description: Add one field that helps you understand what they want: What service are you interested in? What do you need help with?

items.title: Message Field
items.description: Use when you want them to explain their situation. Keep it simple. Do not ask for a full essay.

keyPoint: A good form is clear, short, and connected to the next step. Ask only for what you need right now. People complete forms that feel easy.

actionSteps.title: Audit Your Current Forms
actionSteps.description: Review your existing forms. Are they closer to the good example or the poor example?

actionSteps.title: Count Your Fields
actionSteps.description: How many fields are required? Can you remove any without hurting the follow-up process?

actionSteps.title: Plan a Simple Form
actionSteps.description: Design a form with only the essential fields: Name, Email, Phone, and one interest question.

quizzes.question: What makes a good lead capture form?

options.option_text: Asking for as much information as possible
Being clear, short, and connected to the next step

quizzes.explanation: A good form is clear, short, and connected to the next step. It asks only for what is needed to start a useful conversation.

quizzes.question: What fields should you start with for most lead capture forms?

options.option_text: Full address, company size, budget, website
First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone
Social security number, birth date, mother's maiden name
Credit card number, expiration date, CVV

quizzes.explanation: Start with the basics: First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone. Add one interest field to understand what they want.

quizzes.question: Why do long forms reduce responses?

options.option_text: People are more likely to complete forms when they feel easy

quizzes.explanation: People abandon long, complex forms. Keep forms short and easy to maximize completion rates.

title: Required vs Optional Fields
moduleName: Forms: Capturing Leads the Right Way
learningGoal: Learn which fields should be required and which should be optional to maximize form completion.

items.title: First Name
items.description: You need to know who they are to personalize follow-up.

items.title: Email
items.description: Essential for contact and follow-up communication.

items.title: Main Request or Interest
items.description: You need to know what they want to route them correctly.

items.title: Phone Number
items.description: Important but some people prefer initial contact by email. Consider making optional.

items.title: Longer Message
items.description: Let them share more if they want, but do not require it.

items.title: Company Name & Website
items.description: Useful for B2B but may not be essential for all forms.

items.title: Too Many Required Fields
items.description: If you make too many fields required, some people will leave without submitting.

items.title: The Rule
items.description: Only make a field required if you truly need it before the next step can happen.

keyPoint: Balance information needs with completion rates. Only require fields you absolutely need. Optional fields let interested prospects share more without blocking those who want to move quickly.

actionSteps.title: Review Required Fields
actionSteps.description: Look at your forms. Are any required fields actually optional?

actionSteps.title: Make Phone Optional
actionSteps.description: Consider making phone number optional unless you absolutely need it for the first contact.

actionSteps.title: Test the Change
actionSteps.description: Make fields optional and see if form completion rates improve.

quizzes.question: Which fields should typically be required?

options.option_text: First Name, Email, and Main Request or Interest

quizzes.explanation: Typically require First Name, Email, and the main request or interest field. These are essential for follow-up and routing.

quizzes.question: Why should you consider making phone number optional?

options.option_text: Some people prefer initial contact by email and requiring phone may reduce form completions

quizzes.explanation: Some prospects prefer email first. Making phone optional reduces friction while still capturing it from those willing to share.

quizzes.question: What happens if you make too many fields required?

options.option_text: Some people will leave without submitting the form

quizzes.explanation: Too many required fields creates friction. Some prospects will abandon the form rather than complete all required fields.

title: Button Text That Converts
moduleName: Forms: Capturing Leads the Right Way
learningGoal: Learn how to write button text that tells people exactly what happens next.

items.title: Submit Works But...
items.description: Many forms use 'Submit' as button text. That works, but it is not very clear about what happens next.

items.title: Better Button Text
items.description: Better button wording tells the person what they are doing and what happens next.

items.title: Request My Call
items.description: Perfect for consultation or discovery call forms.

items.title: Send My Request
items.description: Good for general inquiry or quote request forms.

items.title: Get the Guide
items.description: Ideal for lead magnet or download forms.

items.title: Book My Consultation
items.description: Great for calendar booking or appointment forms.

items.title: Join the List
items.description: Perfect for newsletter or email list signups.

items.title: Register Now
items.description: Ideal for event or workshop registration forms.

items.title: Match Button to Purpose
items.description: The button should match the purpose of the form. Tell people exactly what action they are taking.

keyPoint: Button text matters. Clear, action-oriented buttons tell people exactly what happens next and increase form completion rates. Match the button text to your form's purpose.

actionSteps.title: Review Your Button Text
actionSteps.description: Look at your current forms. Do they all say 'Submit'?

actionSteps.title: Choose Better Text
actionSteps.description: Update button text to match what the person is actually doing: requesting, booking, downloading, etc.

actionSteps.title: Test the Change
actionSteps.description: Monitor if clearer button text improves form completion rates.

quizzes.question: Why is 'Submit' not the best button text?

options.option_text: It does not tell people what happens next

quizzes.explanation: 'Submit' is vague. Better button text tells people exactly what action they are taking and what happens next.

quizzes.question: What is a good button text for a consultation form?
quizzes.explanation: 'Request My Call' clearly tells the person what they are doing and what happens next—requesting a call.

quizzes.question: What should button text do?

options.option_text: Match the purpose of the form and tell people what happens next

quizzes.explanation: Button text should match the form's purpose and clearly communicate what action the person is taking and what happens next.

title: What Happens After Submit
moduleName: Forms: Capturing Leads the Right Way
learningGoal: Learn how to set up automated follow-up actions when someone submits a form.

items.title: 1. Contact Created or Updated
items.description: LeadProspectrr automatically creates a new contact or updates an existing one.

items.title: 2. Tag Added
items.description: Add a tag like 'New Lead - Consultation Request' to organize and segment the lead.

items.title: 3. Internal Notification
items.description: Alert yourself or your team that a new lead has come in.

items.title: 4. Thank-You Email
items.description: Send a confirmation email to the lead so they know their request was received.

items.title: 5. Add to Pipeline
items.description: Add the lead to the right pipeline stage if this is a sales or opportunity-based form.

items.title: 6. Start Workflow
items.description: Trigger an automation sequence for nurture, follow-up, or onboarding.

items.title: 7. Redirect to Next Step
items.description: Send the person to a thank-you page, booking calendar, or download page.

keyPoint: The form collects the lead. The follow-up turns that lead into a conversation. Set up automated actions so no lead sits unseen in an inbox.

actionSteps.title: Map Your Follow-Up
actionSteps.description: For each form, list what should happen after someone submits it.

actionSteps.title: Set Up Tags
actionSteps.description: Create clear tags for each form type so you can segment and track leads.

actionSteps.title: Configure Notifications
actionSteps.description: Make sure you or your team get alerted when new leads come in.

actionSteps.title: Create Thank-You Emails
actionSteps.description: Write simple confirmation emails that let leads know their request was received.

quizzes.question: What should happen after someone submits a form?

options.option_text: Nothing, the form just stores the data
Contact creation, tagging, notifications, thank-you emails, pipeline entry, and workflows

quizzes.explanation: After form submission, LeadProspectrr can create contacts, add tags, send notifications and emails, add to pipelines, start workflows, and redirect to next steps.

quizzes.question: Why should you add a tag when someone submits a form?

options.option_text: To organize leads by interest and know where they came from

quizzes.explanation: Tags help you organize leads by interest, track where they came from, and segment them for appropriate follow-up.

quizzes.question: Why is a thank-you email important?

options.option_text: People like to know their request was received and what happens next

quizzes.explanation: A thank-you email confirms the submission was received, sets expectations for follow-up, and starts building trust with the lead.

title: Testing Your Form
moduleName: Forms: Capturing Leads the Right Way
learningGoal: Learn how to thoroughly test forms before publishing them live.

items.title: The Risk
items.description: Never publish a form without testing it first. Testing catches small problems before real leads use the form.

items.title: The Cost
items.description: A broken form can quietly cost you leads. One error can mean lost opportunities.

items.title: Submit Test Lead
items.description: Submit the form as a test lead using a different email address.

items.title: Check Contact Created
items.description: Verify the contact appears in LeadProspectrr with correct information.

items.title: Check Tag Applied
items.description: Confirm the correct tag was added to the contact.

items.title: Check Notification Sent
items.description: Verify internal notifications were sent to you or your team.

items.title: Check Thank-You Email
items.description: Confirm the thank-you email was sent and contains correct information.

items.title: Check Workflow Started
items.description: Verify any workflows were triggered correctly.

items.title: Check Pipeline Updated
items.description: Confirm the lead was added to the correct pipeline stage.

items.title: Check Redirect Works
items.description: Verify the redirect page loads correctly after submission.

items.title: Check Desktop and Mobile
items.description: Test the form on both desktop and mobile devices.

keyPoint: Testing protects your business from losing leads due to broken forms. Always test every field, notification, email, and redirect before going live.

actionSteps.title: Submit Test Lead
actionSteps.description: Fill out your form as if you were a prospect using a test email address.

actionSteps.title: Verify All Actions
actionSteps.description: Check that contact, tag, notification, email, pipeline, and workflow all worked correctly.

actionSteps.title: Test on Mobile
actionSteps.description: Many leads will use mobile devices. Test your form on a phone or tablet.

actionSteps.title: Fix Any Issues
actionSteps.description: If anything does not work, fix it before sharing the form publicly.

quizzes.question: Why should you test a form before publishing it?

options.option_text: To catch problems before real leads use the form

quizzes.explanation: Testing catches errors, broken notifications, missing tags, and other issues before real prospects encounter them.

quizzes.question: What should you check when testing a form?

options.option_text: Contact creation, tags, notifications, emails, workflows, pipeline, and redirect

quizzes.explanation: Thorough testing includes verifying contact creation, tag application, notifications, emails, workflows, pipeline updates, redirects, and mobile compatibility.

quizzes.question: Why test on mobile devices?

options.option_text: Many leads use mobile devices to fill out forms

quizzes.explanation: Many prospects will access your form on mobile devices. Testing ensures the form works properly on all screen sizes.

title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
moduleName: Forms: Capturing Leads the Right Way
learningGoal: Learn the most common form mistakes and how to avoid them.

items.title: Asking for Too Much
items.description: Mistake: Long forms with many fields. Fix: Ask only for what you need right now.

items.title: Vague Button Text
items.description: Mistake: Using 'Submit' on every form. Fix: Use clear action buttons like 'Request My Call'.

items.title: Not Adding Tags
items.description: Mistake: No tags on form submissions. Fix: Tag every form so you know where leads came from.

items.title: No Internal Notification
items.description: Mistake: Nobody gets alerted. Fix: Set up notifications so leads are not missed.

items.title: No Follow-Up Email
items.description: Mistake: No confirmation email. Fix: Send a thank-you email so leads know you received their request.

items.title: No Pipeline Update
items.description: Mistake: Leads not added to pipeline. Fix: Add sales leads to the appropriate pipeline stage.

items.title: Not Testing
items.description: Mistake: Publishing without testing. Fix: Always test before going live.

keyPoint: Most form problems come from rushing the setup. Take time to configure properly, test thoroughly, and review regularly.

actionSteps.title: Review Your Forms
actionSteps.description: Check if you are making any of these common mistakes.

actionSteps.title: Fix One Issue
actionSteps.description: Choose one mistake to fix right now and update your form.

actionSteps.title: Set a Review Schedule
actionSteps.description: Schedule quarterly reviews of your forms to catch and fix issues.

quizzes.question: What is a common mistake when creating forms?
quizzes.explanation: A common mistake is asking for too much information. Long forms reduce completion rates. Ask only for what you truly need.

quizzes.question: Why is not adding tags a mistake?

options.option_text: Without tags, it is harder to know where leads came from or what they wanted

quizzes.explanation: Without tags, you cannot easily segment leads, track their source, or trigger appropriate follow-up workflows.

quizzes.question: What happens if you do not set up internal notifications?

options.option_text: The lead may be missed or sit unseen in the system

quizzes.explanation: Without notifications, you may not know when new leads come in, causing delays in follow-up or missed opportunities entirely.
